::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## 🔁 You already know Kepler's First and Third Laws (Unit 1)

In Unit 1's **Planets and Orbits** chapter you learned:

- **Kepler's First Law:** orbits are **ellipses** with the star at one focus. Eccentricity $e = f/d$ (0 = circle, close to 1 = very stretched). Closest $= R(1-e)$, farthest $= R(1+e)$.
- **Kepler's Third Law:** $M_s \times T^2 = R^3$ (solar masses, Earth years, AU). For our Sun ($M_s = 1$): $T^2 = R^3$.

This chapter adds **Kepler's Second Law** (how *fast* an object moves) and **Newton's Law of Gravitational Force** (*why* it moves that way), then uses all of them to predict where asteroid **Apophis** will be.
:::

# Engage: Asteroids in the Solar System

::: {.engage-box}
## 🌑 Questions from the Driving Question Board

After learning how asteroid impacts caused **mass extinctions**, you asked: **Where do these asteroids come from? How many are still out there? Could another large one hit Earth?**
:::

## Part 1: Where Do Asteroids Come From?

Your packet's video follows a NASA scientist who tracks dangerous asteroids. Here are the key facts it connects to:

| Question | What scientists know |
|---|---|
| **a. Where do asteroids come from?** | Rocky leftovers from the formation of the solar system, about 4.6 billion years ago. Most orbit in the **main asteroid belt** between Mars and Jupiter. **Jupiter's gravity** and collisions nudge some into new orbits that cross Earth's path. These are **near-Earth asteroids**. |
| **b. How many large asteroids are there?** | More than **1 million** asteroids are known, and over **35,000** are near-Earth asteroids. Surveys have found about **95%** of near-Earth asteroids larger than 1 km, but fewer than **half** of those larger than 140 m. |
| **c. Will another large asteroid strike Earth?** | Eventually, yes. Small rocks hit every day and burn up. Large impacts are **rare**, but they do happen. That's why NASA tracks every known near-Earth asteroid's orbit and predicts its path decades ahead. |

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// Shared helpers for this chapter's animated models (controls, canvas sizing, pausing off-screen)
aoKit = {
  const reduce = !!(window.matchMedia && window.matchMedia("(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)").matches);
  let uid = 0;
  const h = (tag, props = {}, kids = []) => {
    const n = document.createElement(tag);
    for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(props)) {
      if (k === "style") n.style.cssText = v;
      else if (k === "text") n.textContent = v;
      else if (k === "html") n.innerHTML = v;
      else if (k === "className") n.className = v;
      else n.setAttribute(k, v);
    }
    for (const c of [].concat(kids)) if (c) n.append(c);
    return n;
  };
  const slider = ({label, min, max, step, value, fmt = v => String(v)}) => {
    const id = "ao-sl-" + (++uid);
    const input = h("input", {type: "range", id, min, max, step});
    input.value = value;
    const out = h("output", {for: id});
    const row = h("div", {className: "ao-sim-row"}, [h("label", {for: id, text: label}), input, out]);
    const sync = () => { out.textContent = fmt(+input.value); };
    input.addEventListener("input", sync);
    sync();
    return {row, input, sync, get value() { return +input.value; }, set value(v) { input.value = v; sync(); }};
  };
  const button = (text, pressed) => {
    const b = h("button", {type: "button", className: "ao-sim-btn", text});
    if (pressed !== undefined) b.setAttribute("aria-pressed", String(pressed));
    return b;
  };
  const readout = label => {
    const b = h("b"), node = h("div", {}, [b, label]);
    return {node, set(t) { if (b.textContent !== t) b.textContent = t; }};
  };
  // 2D canvas with a fixed logical size (W x H); the backing store follows the real width, device pixel ratio capped at 2
  const canvas2d = (W, H, label) => {
    const c = h("canvas", {role: "img", "aria-label": label, width: W, height: H});
    c.style.aspectRatio = `${W} / ${H}`;
    const ctx = c.getContext("2d");
    const fit = () => {
      const dpr = Math.min(window.devicePixelRatio || 1, 2);
      const bw = Math.max(1, Math.round((c.clientWidth || W) * dpr));
      if (c.width !== bw) { c.width = bw; c.height = Math.round(bw * H / W); }
      ctx.setTransform(c.width / W, 0, 0, c.width / W, 0, 0);
    };
    return {c, ctx, fit};
  };
  // Animation loop that only runs while playing AND on screen; stops for good when the cell is invalidated
  const runner = (target, tick, draw, invalidation) => {
    let raf = 0, visible = false, playing = false, last = 0;
    const frame = ts => {
      raf = 0;
      const dt = Math.min(Math.max((ts - last) / 1000, 0), 0.05);
      last = ts;
      tick(dt);
      draw();
      if (visible && playing) raf = requestAnimationFrame(frame);
    };
    const kick = () => { if (visible && playing && !raf) { last = performance.now(); raf = requestAnimationFrame(frame); } };
    const halt = () => { if (raf) cancelAnimationFrame(raf); raf = 0; };
    const io = new IntersectionObserver(es => { visible = es[es.length - 1].isIntersecting; if (visible) kick(); else halt(); });
    io.observe(target);
    const ro = new ResizeObserver(() => draw());
    ro.observe(target);
    invalidation.then(() => { halt(); io.disconnect(); ro.disconnect(); });
    return {play() { playing = true; kick(); }, pause() { playing = false; halt(); }, get playing() { return playing; }};
  };
  const arrow = (ctx, x1, y1, x2, y2, color, w = 2.5) => {
    const a = Math.atan2(y2 - y1, x2 - x1), hd = 7;
    ctx.strokeStyle = color; ctx.fillStyle = color; ctx.lineWidth = w; ctx.lineCap = "round";
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(x1, y1); ctx.lineTo(x2 - Math.cos(a) * hd * 0.7, y2 - Math.sin(a) * hd * 0.7); ctx.stroke();
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(x2, y2);
    ctx.lineTo(x2 - hd * Math.cos(a - 0.45), y2 - hd * Math.sin(a - 0.45));
    ctx.lineTo(x2 - hd * Math.cos(a + 0.45), y2 - hd * Math.sin(a + 0.45));
    ctx.closePath(); ctx.fill();
  };
  // Fixed decorative background stars (same every time, not data)
  const stars = (ctx, W, H, n = 60) => {
    let s = 12345;
    const rnd = () => (s = (s * 16807) % 2147483647) / 2147483647;
    ctx.fillStyle = "rgba(255,255,255,.45)";
    for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) { const r = rnd() < 0.15 ? 1 : 0.6; ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(rnd() * W, rnd() * H, r, 0, 7); ctx.fill(); }
  };
  return {reduce, h, slider, button, readout, canvas2d, runner, arrow, stars};
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
buildQuiz = function(id, title, questions) {
  const outer = html`<div id="${id}" style="margin:18px 0 24px 0;text-align:center;">
    <button style="
      display:inline-flex;align-items:center;gap:7px;
      background:linear-gradient(135deg,#667eea 0%,#764ba2 100%);
      color:#fff;border:none;padding:9px 22px;border-radius:50px;
      font-size:.95em;font-weight:700;cursor:pointer;
      box-shadow:0 3px 12px rgba(102,126,234,.45);
      transition:transform .15s,box-shadow .15s;"
      onmouseover="this.style.transform='scale(1.04)';this.style.boxShadow='0 5px 18px rgba(102,126,234,.55)'"
      onmouseout="this.style.transform='scale(1)';this.style.boxShadow='0 3px 12px rgba(102,126,234,.45)'"
    >
      <span style="font-size:1.1em;">📝</span> ${title}
      <span class="chevron" style="transition:transform .3s;">▼</span>
    </button>
    <div class="quiz-body" style="
      max-height:0;opacity:0;overflow:hidden;
      transition:max-height .5s cubic-bezier(.4,0,.2,1),opacity .4s ease,margin-top .3s ease;
      margin-top:0;text-align:left;">
      <button class="close-btn" style="
        display:block;margin:0 auto 10px auto;
        background:rgba(102,126,234,.12);color:#667eea;border:none;
        padding:5px 18px;border-radius:50px;font-size:.85em;
        font-weight:600;cursor:pointer;">Hide Quiz</button>
      <p style="text-align:center;color:#718096;font-style:italic;font-size:.9em;margin-bottom:12px;">
        Select an answer for each question.</p>
    </div>
  </div>`;
  const toggle = outer.querySelector("button");
  const chevron = toggle.querySelector(".chevron");
  const body   = outer.querySelector(".quiz-body");
  const closeBtn = body.querySelector(".close-btn");
  function expand(){  body.style.maxHeight="2000px";body.style.opacity="1";body.style.marginTop="14px";chevron.style.transform="rotate(180deg)"; }
  function collapse(){ body.style.maxHeight="0";body.style.opacity="0";body.style.marginTop="0";chevron.style.transform="rotate(0)"; }
  toggle.onclick = () => body.style.maxHeight === "0px" || body.style.maxHeight === "" ? expand() : collapse();
  closeBtn.onclick = collapse;
  questions.forEach((qq, qi) => {
    const card = document.createElement("div");
    card.style.cssText = "background:#fff;color:#1e1b4b;border-radius:12px;padding:16px 20px;margin-bottom:14px;box-shadow:0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,.08);";
    card.innerHTML = `<p style="font-weight:700;margin:0 0 10px;">${qi+1}. ${qq.q}</p>`;
    qq.options.forEach((opt, oi) => {
      const btn = document.createElement("button");
      btn.textContent = opt;
      btn.style.cssText = "display:block;width:100%;min-height:44px;text-align:left;padding:10px 14px;margin:6px 0;border:2px solid #e2e8f0;border-radius:8px;background:#fff;color:#1e1b4b;cursor:pointer;font-size:.95em;transition:border-color .2s,background .2s;";
      btn.onmouseover = () => { if(!card.dataset.answered){ btn.style.borderColor="#667eea";btn.style.background="#f0f0ff"; }};
      btn.onmouseout  = () => { if(!card.dataset.answered){ btn.style.borderColor="#e2e8f0";btn.style.background="#fff"; }};
      btn.onclick = () => {
        if(card.dataset.answered) return;
        card.dataset.answered = "true";
        card.querySelectorAll("button").forEach(b => { b.style.cursor="default"; b.onmouseover=null; b.onmouseout=null; });
        if(oi === qq.correct){
          btn.style.borderColor="#48bb78";btn.style.background="#f0fff4";
          fb.innerHTML = "✅ Correct! " + qq.explanation;
          fb.style.color="#276749";fb.style.background="#f0fff4";
        } else {
          btn.style.borderColor="#fc8181";btn.style.background="#fff5f5";
          card.querySelectorAll("button")[qq.correct].style.borderColor="#48bb78";
          card.querySelectorAll("button")[qq.correct].style.background="#f0fff4";
          fb.innerHTML = "❌ " + qq.explanation;
          fb.style.color="#9b2c2c";fb.style.background="#fff5f5";
        }
        fb.style.padding="10px 14px";fb.style.marginTop="8px";
      };
      card.appendChild(btn);
    });
    const fb = document.createElement("div");
    fb.style.cssText = "border-radius:8px;font-size:.9em;transition:all .3s;";
    card.appendChild(fb);
    body.appendChild(card);
  });
  return outer;
}
```

```{ojs}
buildQuiz("ao-engage-quiz", "☄️ Check Your Understanding — Asteroids in the Solar System", [
  {
    q: "Where do most asteroids in our solar system orbit?",
    options: ["In the main asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter", "Between Earth and the Moon", "Beyond Pluto only", "Inside Mercury's orbit"],
    correct: 0,
    explanation: "Most asteroids are rocky leftovers from the solar system's formation and orbit in the main belt between Mars and Jupiter. Jupiter's gravity and collisions can nudge some into orbits that cross Earth's."
  },
  {
    q: "Look at the survey chart. Which size group still has the MOST undiscovered near-Earth asteroids?",
    options: ["Larger than 1 km", "Larger than 140 m", "Both groups are completely found", "Neither group has been searched"],
    correct: 1,
    explanation: "About 95% of the 1 km+ asteroids are found, but only around 11,000 of an estimated 25,000 asteroids larger than 140 m have been found. That's why surveys keep searching."
  },
  {
    q: "According to the impact chart, how does an asteroid's size relate to how often one that size hits Earth?",
    options: ["Bigger asteroids hit more often", "Size doesn't matter", "Bigger asteroids hit much less often", "Only small asteroids ever hit Earth"],
    correct: 2,
    explanation: "Small asteroids are common, so they hit often. Large ones are rare: a ~10 km impact (like the one linked to the dinosaur extinction) happens only about once every 100 million years."
  }
])
```

## Part 2: Apophis

::: {.engage-box}
## 🗓️ Friday, April 13, 2029

Asteroid **99942 Apophis** is about **340 m** (1,100 ft) across, about the length of three football fields. On **April 13, 2029** it will pass less than **32,000 km** above Earth's surface. That's closer than the satellites in geostationary orbit, and it will be visible **without a telescope** from parts of Europe, Africa, and Asia.

When it was discovered in **2004**, early calculations gave a **2.7% chance** it would hit Earth in 2029. Better measurements of its orbit ruled that out, and in 2021 radar tracking ruled out any impact for at least the next 100 years.
:::

  <img src="https://images-assets.nasa.gov/image/PIA24168/PIA24168~medium.jpg"
       alt="Three grainy radar images of asteroid Apophis taken in March 2021, showing a lumpy, elongated rocky body"
       style="width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 12px; box-shadow: 0 6px 20px rgba(0,0,0,.25);">
  <figcaption style="margin-top: 8px; color: #64748b; font-size: .85em; font-style: italic; line-height: 1.4;">
    Radar images of Apophis from NASA's Goldstone antenna and the Green Bank Telescope, March 2021. These measurements pinned down its orbit precisely enough to rule out an impact for at least 100 years. Credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech and NSF/AUI/GBO.
  </figcaption>
</figure>

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
```
```{ojs}
{
  // To-scale strip: distance above Earth's surface runs left to right.
  const zoom = aoScaleView !== "Earth to the Moon";
  const W = 360, H = 170, MID = 92, X0 = zoom ? 46 : 20, maxKm = zoom ? 42000 : 400000;
  const k = (W - X0 - 22) / maxKm, x = km => X0 + km * k, rE = 6371 * k;
  const col = {Satellite: "#74b9ff", Asteroid: "#ff7675", Moon: "#dfe6e9"};
  const svg = d3.create("svg").attr("viewBox", `0 0 ${W} ${H}`).attr("role", "img")
    .attr("aria-label", "Scale diagram of distances above Earth: the International Space Station at 420 km, GPS satellites at 20,200 km, Apophis in 2029 at 32,000 km, geostationary satellites at 35,786 km, and the Moon at 384,400 km. Apophis passes about twelve times closer than the Moon, inside the ring of geostationary satellites.")
    .style("width", "100%").style("height", "auto").style("max-width", "680px").style("display", "block").style("margin", "6px auto 0");
  svg.append("clipPath").attr("id", "ao-scale-clip").append("rect").attr("width", W).attr("height", H).attr("rx", 12);
  const g = svg.append("g").attr("clip-path", "url(#ao-scale-clip)");
  g.append("rect").attr("width", W).attr("height", H).attr("fill", "#0b1026");
  const text = (tx, ty, s, o = {}) => g.append("text").attr("x", tx).attr("y", ty).attr("text-anchor", o.anchor || "middle")
    .attr("font-size", o.size || 9.5).attr("font-weight", o.bold ? "bold" : "normal").attr("fill", o.fill || "#dfe6e9").text(s);
  text(W / 2, 16, zoom ? "Zoomed in: the first 42,000 km above Earth" : "Earth to the Moon, drawn to scale", {bold: true, size: 11, fill: "#fff"});
  g.append("line").attr("x1", x(0)).attr("x2", W).attr("y1", MID).attr("y2", MID).attr("stroke", "#4b5a86").attr("stroke-dasharray", "2,3");
  g.append("circle").attr("cx", x(0) - rE).attr("cy", MID).attr("r", Math.max(rE, 2)).attr("fill", "#2e86de").attr("stroke", "#7bed9f").attr("stroke-width", zoom ? 2 : 0.8);
  if (zoom) {
    text(x(0) - 6, MID + 4, "Earth", {anchor: "end", bold: true, fill: "#fff"});
    // label positions: [row above/below the line, text anchor]
    const lay = {"International Space Station": [-1, "start", "ISS"], "GPS satellites": [1, "middle", "GPS satellites"],
      "Apophis on April 13, 2029": [-1, "middle", "Apophis, 2029"], "Geostationary satellites": [1, "middle", "Geostationary"]};
    approachData.filter(d => lay[d.name]).forEach(d => {
      const [side, anchor, label] = lay[d.name], px = x(d.distance), ast = d.kind === "Asteroid";
      g.append("line").attr("x1", px).attr("x2", px).attr("y1", MID).attr("y2", MID + side * 30).attr("stroke", col[d.kind]).attr("stroke-width", 1);
      g.append("circle").attr("cx", px).attr("cy", MID).attr("r", ast ? 4.5 : 3).attr("fill", col[d.kind]);
      text(px, MID + side * 30 + (side < 0 ? -15 : 11), label, {anchor, bold: true, fill: col[d.kind]});
      text(px, MID + side * 30 + (side < 0 ? -4 : 22), d.distance.toLocaleString() + " km", {anchor, size: 9});
    });
    text(W - 8, 31, "The Moon is 9× farther this way →", {anchor: "end", size: 9, fill: "#b2bec3"});
  } else {
    const moon = approachData.find(d => d.kind === "Moon"), geo = approachData.find(d => d.name.startsWith("Geostationary")), ap = approachData.find(d => d.kind === "Asteroid");
    g.append("circle").attr("cx", x(moon.distance)).attr("cy", MID).attr("r", 2.6).attr("fill", col.Moon);
    text(x(moon.distance), MID - 12, "Moon", {bold: true, fill: "#fff"});
    text(x(moon.distance) + 8, MID + 18, moon.distance.toLocaleString() + " km", {anchor: "end", size: 9});
    g.append("rect").attr("x", x(0)).attr("y", MID - 7).attr("width", x(geo.distance) - x(0)).attr("height", 14).attr("fill", "#74b9ff").attr("opacity", 0.3);
    g.append("circle").attr("cx", x(ap.distance)).attr("cy", MID).attr("r", 3).attr("fill", col.Asteroid);
    g.append("path").attr("d", `M${x(ap.distance)},${MID + 6} L${x(ap.distance) + 22},${MID + 34}`).attr("stroke", col.Asteroid).attr("stroke-width", 1).attr("fill", "none");
    text(x(ap.distance) + 26, MID + 40, "Apophis, 2029: " + ap.distance.toLocaleString() + " km", {anchor: "start", bold: true, fill: col.Asteroid});
    text(x(ap.distance) + 26, MID + 52, "All our satellites orbit in this thin blue band.", {anchor: "start", size: 9});
    text(x(0) - rE, MID - 14, "Earth", {anchor: "start", bold: true, fill: "#fff"});
  }
  text(W / 2, H - 8, "Earth and the distances are to scale. The other dots are enlarged.", {size: 8, fill: "#b2bec3"});
  return svg.node();
}
```

# Explore: Asteroid Paths and Velocities Investigation

::: {.explore-box}
## 🔬 Different Objects, Different Paths

The shape of Pluto's orbit was one of the reasons it was reclassified as a **dwarf planet** in 2006. By understanding the paths and speeds of objects in space, we can predict whether an asteroid will hit Earth or miss.

- **Part 1** revisits **Kepler's First Law** (orbit shape) and discovers **Kepler's Second Law** (orbit speed).
- **Part 2** adds the **force of gravity** as the *cause* of these patterns.
:::

## Part 1: Motion of Asteroids and Comets

All objects in the solar system move in **ellipses**. Planets' ellipses are nearly circles, but asteroids and comets can have very stretched orbits. This lab works like the packet's *Kepler's Second Law* simulation:

- Change the **eccentricity**: what happens to the shape?
- Set eccentricity **0.7** and semi-major axis **3 AU**. Each colored wedge is the area swept by the line from the Sun to the object in **1/16 of its orbit**.
- Press **Play** and watch **your sweep** (blue) follow the object. Its shape keeps changing. Does its **area** change?
- Press **Pause** and use the last slider to park the object anywhere. Compare your sweep with the other two in the table.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
aoSolveE = (M, e) => { let E = e > 0.8 ? Math.PI : M; for (let i = 0; i < 30; i++) E = E - (E - e * Math.sin(E) - M) / (1 - e * Math.cos(E)); return E; }
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
aoK2Sim = {
  const K = aoKit, W = 360, H = 250, TAU = 2 * Math.PI;
  const cv = K.canvas2d(W, H, "Animated model of an object orbiting the Sun on an ellipse, with the Sun at one focus. Three colored wedges each show the area swept in one sixteenth of the orbit: one near the Sun, one far from the Sun, and one that trails the moving object.");
  const ctx = cv.ctx;
  const sE = K.slider({label: "Eccentricity", min: 0, max: 0.9, step: 0.01, value: 0.7, fmt: v => v.toFixed(2)});
  const sA = K.slider({label: "Semi-major axis (AU)", min: 0.5, max: 5, step: 0.01, value: 3, fmt: v => v.toFixed(2)});
  const sP = K.slider({label: "Move the object (fraction of one orbit after its closest point)", min: 0, max: 1, step: 0.005, value: 0.25, fmt: v => v.toFixed(2)});
  const bPlay = K.button(K.reduce ? "▶ Play" : "⏸ Pause");
  const rR = K.readout("Distance from the Sun now"), rV = K.readout("Speed now"), rT = K.readout("Time for one full orbit");
  const sweeps = [
    {name: "Near the Sun", color: "#f1c40f"},
    {name: "Far from the Sun", color: "#e84393"},
    {name: "Your sweep", color: "#00cec9"}
  ];
  const tbody = K.h("tbody");
  for (const sw of sweeps) {
    sw.cells = [0, 1, 2, 3].map(() => K.h("td"));
    tbody.append(K.h("tr", {}, [K.h("td", {}, [K.h("span", {className: "ao-sim-dot", style: `background:${sw.color}`}), sw.name]), ...sw.cells]));
  }
  const table = K.h("div", {className: "ao-sim-tablewrap"}, K.h("table", {}, [
    K.h("thead", {}, K.h("tr", {}, ["Sweep", "Time (yr)", "Area (AU²)", "Distance traveled (AU)", "Average speed (km/s)"].map(t => K.h("th", {text: t})))),
    tbody]));
  const root = K.h("div", {className: "ao-sim"}, [
    K.h("div", {className: "ao-sim-title", text: "Model: Kepler's Second Law"}),
    cv.c,
    K.h("div", {className: "ao-sim-btns"}, [bPlay]),
    sE.row, sA.row, sP.row,
    K.h("div", {className: "ao-sim-read"}, [rR.node, rV.node, rT.node]),
    table,
    K.h("div", {className: "ao-sim-note", text: "This is a mathematical model built from Kepler's laws for an object orbiting our Sun. Each wedge covers 1/16 of the orbit's time. The green arrow shows the object's speed and direction. The picture is zoomed to fit, so use the scale bar."})
  ]);

  let frac = 0.25;
  const pos = (M, a, e) => {
    const E = aoSolveE(((M % TAU) + TAU) % TAU, e);
    return {x: a * (Math.cos(E) - e), y: a * Math.sqrt(1 - e * e) * Math.sin(E)};
  };
  const sweep = (M0, a, e, T) => {
    const pts = [];
    for (let i = 0; i <= 60; i++) pts.push(pos(M0 + (i / 60) * TAU / 16, a, e));
    let arc = 0, area = 0;
    for (let i = 1; i < pts.length; i++) {
      arc += Math.hypot(pts[i].x - pts[i - 1].x, pts[i].y - pts[i - 1].y);
      area += 0.5 * Math.abs(pts[i - 1].x * pts[i].y - pts[i].x * pts[i - 1].y);   // thin triangle from the Sun
    }
    return {pts, arc, area, dur: T / 16, speed: arc / (T / 16) * 4.74};
  };
  function draw() {
    cv.fit();
    const a = sA.value, e = sE.value, b = a * Math.sqrt(1 - e * e), T = Math.pow(a, 1.5);
    const s = Math.min((W - 36) / (2 * a), (H - 74) / (2 * b));
    const sunX = W / 2 + a * e * s, sunY = H / 2 + 6;
    const X = p => sunX + p.x * s, Y = p => sunY - p.y * s;
    ctx.fillStyle = "#0a0a2e"; ctx.fillRect(0, 0, W, H);
    K.stars(ctx, W, H);
    ctx.strokeStyle = "#9aa7bd"; ctx.lineWidth = 1.2;
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.ellipse(sunX - a * e * s, sunY, a * s, b * s, 0, 0, TAU); ctx.stroke();
    const starts = [-Math.PI / 16, Math.PI - Math.PI / 16, TAU * (frac - 1 / 16)];
    sweeps.forEach((sw, i) => {
      const r = sweep(starts[i], a, e, T);
      ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(sunX, sunY);
      for (const p of r.pts) ctx.lineTo(X(p), Y(p));
      ctx.closePath();
      ctx.globalAlpha = 0.5; ctx.fillStyle = sw.color; ctx.fill();
      ctx.globalAlpha = 1; ctx.strokeStyle = sw.color; ctx.lineWidth = 1; ctx.stroke();
      [r.dur.toFixed(4), r.area.toFixed(3), r.arc.toFixed(3), r.speed.toFixed(1)].forEach((t, j) => { if (sw.cells[j].textContent !== t) sw.cells[j].textContent = t; });
    });
    ctx.fillStyle = "#f39c12"; ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(sunX, sunY, 6, 0, TAU); ctx.fill();
    const p = pos(TAU * frac, a, e), q = pos(TAU * frac + 0.002, a, e);
    const r = Math.hypot(p.x, p.y), v = 29.78 * Math.sqrt(Math.max(2 / r - 1 / a, 0));
    const dx = q.x - p.x, dy = q.y - p.y, dl = Math.hypot(dx, dy) || 1, al = Math.min(12 + v * 0.9, 70);
    K.arrow(ctx, X(p), Y(p), X(p) + dx / dl * al, Y(p) - dy / dl * al, "#2ecc71");
    ctx.fillStyle = "#fff"; ctx.strokeStyle = "#00cec9"; ctx.lineWidth = 2;
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(X(p), Y(p), 5, 0, TAU); ctx.fill(); ctx.stroke();
    // scale bar
    const bar = s <= 110 ? 1 : s <= 220 ? 0.5 : 0.25;
    ctx.strokeStyle = "#e2e8f0"; ctx.lineWidth = 2; ctx.beginPath();
    ctx.moveTo(12, H - 14); ctx.lineTo(12 + bar * s, H - 14); ctx.stroke();
    ctx.fillStyle = "#e2e8f0"; ctx.font = "11px sans-serif"; ctx.textBaseline = "middle"; ctx.textAlign = "left";
    ctx.fillText(bar + " AU", 18 + bar * s, H - 14);
    ctx.font = "bold 11px sans-serif"; ctx.fillStyle = "#fff";
    ctx.fillText(`e = ${e.toFixed(2)}    a = ${a.toFixed(2)} AU`, 10, 14);
    rR.set(r.toFixed(2) + " AU"); rV.set(v.toFixed(1) + " km/s"); rT.set(T.toFixed(2) + " years");
  }
  const run = K.runner(root, dt => { frac = (frac + dt / 9) % 1; sP.value = frac; }, draw, invalidation);
  bPlay.onclick = () => { if (run.playing) { run.pause(); bPlay.textContent = "▶ Play"; } else { run.play(); bPlay.textContent = "⏸ Pause"; } };
  sP.input.addEventListener("input", () => { run.pause(); bPlay.textContent = "▶ Play"; frac = sP.value % 1; draw(); });
  sE.input.addEventListener("input", draw);
  sA.input.addEventListener("input", draw);
  draw();
  if (!K.reduce) run.play();
  return root;
}
```

::: {.callout-tip}
## 📸 Match the packet picture

The packet shows two sweeps that **both lasted 0.0479 years** and **both covered 0.104 AU²**. Set **a = 0.84 AU** and **e = 0.65**: you'll get nearly the same numbers. Same time, same area, but very different distances traveled!
:::

## Part 2: The Force of Gravity

### Gravity: mass and distance

Like the packet's *Gravity* simulation, change the masses and the distance between two objects. (Units are simplified so that the starting force is 1.)

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof gM1 = Inputs.range([1, 10], {label: "Mass of object 1:", step: 1, value: 1})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof gM2 = Inputs.range([1, 10], {label: "Mass of object 2:", step: 1, value: 1})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof gR = Inputs.range([1, 5], {label: "Distance between centers:", step: 0.5, value: 1})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const F = gM1 * gM2 / (gR * gR);
  const curve = d3.range(1, 5.01, 0.05).map(r => ({r, F: gM1 * gM2 / (r * r)}));
  const wrap = d3.create("div");
  wrap.append("div").style("padding", "10px 14px").style("border-radius", "10px").style("margin-bottom", "8px")
    .style("background", "rgba(0,131,143,0.1)").style("border-left", "4px solid #00838f")
    .html(`<strong>Force of gravity = ${+F.toFixed(3)}</strong> (starting force = 1). ` +
      `Masses multiplied: ${gM1} × ${gM2} = ${gM1 * gM2}. Distance squared: ${gR}² = ${gR * gR}.`);
  wrap.append(() => Plot.plot({
    title: "Force of gravity vs. distance (for these masses)",
    width: width, height: 260, marginLeft: 48, marginBottom: 40,
    x: {label: "Distance between centers", grid: true},
    y: {label: "Force of gravity", grid: true},
    marks: [
      Plot.line(curve, {x: "r", y: "F", stroke: "#6c5ce7", strokeWidth: 2}),
      Plot.dot([{r: gR, F}], {x: "r", y: "F", r: 7, fill: "#d63031", tip: true})
    ]
  }));
  return wrap.node();
}
```

### Gravity and orbits

Like the packet's *Gravity and Orbits* simulation: a planet starts 1 AU from its star, moving at Earth's speed. **Change the star's mass** and watch the path. The **blue arrow** is the gravity force (toward the star); the **green arrow** is the velocity. Then try a different **planet mass** or **starting speed**. Each change to the star or the speed restarts the planet from the same spot, so you can compare paths fairly.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
aoGOSim = {
  const K = aoKit, W = 360, H = 320, TAU = 2 * Math.PI, S = 84, CX = 250, CY = 160;
  const cv = K.canvas2d(W, H, "Animated physics model of a planet orbiting a star. A blue arrow shows the gravity force pointing at the star, a green arrow shows the planet's velocity, and a purple line traces the path.");
  const ctx = cv.ctx;
  const sM = K.slider({label: "Star mass (× Sun)", min: 0.7, max: 2, step: 0.05, value: 1, fmt: v => v.toFixed(2)});
  const sP = K.slider({label: "Planet mass (× Earth)", min: 0.5, max: 3, step: 0.5, value: 1, fmt: v => v.toFixed(1)});
  const sV = K.slider({label: "Starting speed (× Earth's speed)", min: 0.6, max: 1.2, step: 0.05, value: 1, fmt: v => v.toFixed(2)});
  const bPlay = K.button(K.reduce ? "▶ Play" : "⏸ Pause"), bReset = K.button("↺ Restart");
  const show = {force: true, vel: true, path: true};
  const toggles = [["force", "Gravity force", "#4aa3ff"], ["vel", "Velocity", "#2ecc71"], ["path", "Path", "#a29bfe"]].map(([key, text, color]) => {
    const b = K.button(text, true);
    b.prepend(K.h("span", {className: "ao-sim-dot", style: `background:${color}`}));
    b.onclick = () => { show[key] = !show[key]; b.setAttribute("aria-pressed", String(show[key])); draw(); };
    return b;
  });
  const rD = K.readout("Distance from the star"), rF = K.readout("Gravity force (× today's Sun-Earth force)"), rS = K.readout("Speed");
  const status = K.h("div", {className: "ao-sim-status", role: "status"});
  const root = K.h("div", {className: "ao-sim"}, [
    K.h("div", {className: "ao-sim-title", text: "Model: gravity and orbits"}),
    cv.c,
    K.h("div", {className: "ao-sim-btns"}, [bPlay, bReset, ...toggles]),
    sM.row, sP.row, sV.row,
    K.h("div", {className: "ao-sim-read"}, [rD.node, rF.node, rS.node]),
    status,
    K.h("div", {className: "ao-sim-note", text: "This is a physics model, not real data. Each instant, the computer uses F = G·m₁·m₂/r² to work out the pull, then moves the planet a tiny step. The planet always starts 1 AU from the star. Sizes are not to scale."})
  ]);

  let x, y, vx, vy, pts, done;
  const mu = () => 4 * Math.PI * Math.PI * sM.value;          // AU³/yr², so Earth's speed is 2π AU/yr
  function reset() { x = 1; y = 0; vx = 0; vy = TAU * sV.value; pts = []; done = false; }
  function tick(dt) {
    if (done) return;
    const m = mu(), steps = 40, h = (dt * 0.35) / steps;     // 0.35 model years per second
    for (let i = 0; i < steps; i++) {
      let r3 = Math.pow(x * x + y * y, 1.5);
      vx -= m * x / r3 * h / 2; vy -= m * y / r3 * h / 2;
      x += vx * h; y += vy * h;
      r3 = Math.pow(x * x + y * y, 1.5);
      vx -= m * x / r3 * h / 2; vy -= m * y / r3 * h / 2;
    }
    pts.push(CX + x * S, CY - y * S);
    if (pts.length > 5000) pts.splice(0, 2);
    if (Math.hypot(x, y) > 12) done = true;
  }
  function draw() {
    cv.fit();
    const M = sM.value, mp = sP.value, m = mu();
    ctx.fillStyle = "#0a0a2e"; ctx.fillRect(0, 0, W, H);
    K.stars(ctx, W, H);
    // faint reference circle: 1 AU from the star
    ctx.strokeStyle = "rgba(255,255,255,.22)"; ctx.setLineDash([3, 4]); ctx.lineWidth = 1;
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(CX, CY, S, 0, TAU); ctx.stroke(); ctx.setLineDash([]);
    ctx.fillStyle = "rgba(255,255,255,.6)"; ctx.font = "10.5px sans-serif"; ctx.textAlign = "center"; ctx.textBaseline = "alphabetic";
    ctx.fillText("1 AU from the star", CX, CY + S + 12);
    if (show.path && pts.length > 3) {
      ctx.strokeStyle = "#a29bfe"; ctx.lineWidth = 1.4; ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(pts[0], pts[1]);
      for (let i = 2; i < pts.length; i += 2) ctx.lineTo(pts[i], pts[i + 1]);
      ctx.stroke();
    }
    const g = ctx.createRadialGradient(CX, CY, 1, CX, CY, 14 + 8 * M);
    g.addColorStop(0, "rgba(255,200,80,.55)"); g.addColorStop(1, "rgba(255,200,80,0)");
    ctx.fillStyle = g; ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(CX, CY, 14 + 8 * M, 0, TAU); ctx.fill();
    ctx.fillStyle = "#f39c12"; ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(CX, CY, 5 + 3 * M, 0, TAU); ctx.fill();
    const r = Math.hypot(x, y), v = Math.hypot(vx, vy), Frel = M * mp / (r * r);
    const px = CX + x * S, py = CY - y * S;
    if (show.force) { const fl = Math.min(14 + 20 * Frel, 100); K.arrow(ctx, px, py, px - (x / r) * fl, py + (y / r) * fl, "#4aa3ff"); }
    if (show.vel) { const vl = 12 + 20 * (v / TAU); K.arrow(ctx, px, py, px + (vx / v) * vl, py - (vy / v) * vl, "#2ecc71"); }
    ctx.fillStyle = "#74b9ff"; ctx.strokeStyle = "#fff"; ctx.lineWidth = 1;
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(px, py, 3 + 1.3 * mp, 0, TAU); ctx.fill(); ctx.stroke();
    rD.set(r.toFixed(2) + " AU"); rF.set(Frel.toFixed(2) + " ×"); rS.set((v * 4.74).toFixed(1) + " km/s");
    const energy = v * v / 2 - m / r, hh = x * vy - y * vx, ecc = Math.sqrt(Math.max(0, 1 + 2 * energy * hh * hh / (m * m)));
    status.textContent = energy >= 0 ? "The planet escapes! At this speed the star's gravity is too weak to hold it."
      : ecc < 0.02 ? "The path is a circle: distance, force, and speed stay the same."
      : `The path is an ellipse (eccentricity ${ecc.toFixed(2)}). Watch the arrows change as the planet moves in and out.`;
  }
  const run = K.runner(root, tick, draw, invalidation);
  bPlay.onclick = () => { if (run.playing) { run.pause(); bPlay.textContent = "▶ Play"; } else { run.play(); bPlay.textContent = "⏸ Pause"; } };
  const restart = () => { reset(); draw(); };
  bReset.onclick = restart;
  sM.input.addEventListener("input", restart);
  sV.input.addEventListener("input", restart);
  sP.input.addEventListener("input", draw);
  reset(); draw();
  if (!K.reduce) run.play();
  return root;
}
```

# Explain: Mathematical Modeling of Orbital Stability and Change

::: {.explain-box}
## 🧠 Turning Patterns into Mathematical Models

You observed two patterns: objects **sweep equal areas in equal times**, and they **move faster closer to the Sun**. Now we write those patterns as equations, and use **gravity** to explain *why* they happen.
:::

## Part 1: Describing and Explaining Orbital Motion

::: {.key-idea}
### 💡 Kepler's Second Law of Planetary Motion

**Mathematical models:**

$$\frac{A}{t} = C \qquad\qquad r \times v = C$$

- $A$ = area swept by the line from the star to the object; $t$ = duration of the sweep; $C$ = a constant (stays the same for that orbit)
- $r$ = distance between the centers of mass (object to star); $v$ = orbital velocity (speed)

**Verbal models:**

- A line from the star to an orbiting object **sweeps out equal areas in equal amounts of time**.
- An object's distance and speed are linked: **when the distance gets smaller, the speed gets bigger** (and vice versa), so that the area swept each day stays the same.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## 📝 About the packet's "r = Cw" box

Your packet writes the second model as **r = Cw** (*"constant and orbital velocity multiplied"*). The physics behind that box is the relationship above: at the closest and farthest points of an orbit, **distance × speed = the same constant**, which you can rewrite as $r = C \div v$. However it's written, the key idea is an **inverse** relationship: **closer → faster, farther → slower**. That is exactly what your sweeps showed.
:::

The chart below uses real orbits: **Earth**, asteroid **Apophis**, and **Comet Borrelly** (from Unit 1). Each curve shows the object's speed at every distance it reaches.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false

  {name: "Earth", a: 1.0, e: 0.0167, color: "#2ecc71"},
  {name: "Apophis", a: 0.922, e: 0.191, color: "#d63031"},
  {name: "Comet Borrelly", a: 3.59, e: 0.624, color: "#6c5ce7"}
]
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const speed = (r, a) => 29.78 * Math.sqrt(2 / r - 1 / a);   // km/s around the Sun
  const curves = aoBodies.flatMap(b => d3.range(0, 1.0001, 0.01).map(f => {
    const r = b.a * (1 - b.e) + f * 2 * b.a * b.e;
    return {name: b.name, r, v: speed(r, b.a)};
  }));
  const ends = aoBodies.flatMap(b => [["closest", b.a * (1 - b.e)], ["farthest", b.a * (1 + b.e)]].map(([k, r]) =>
    ({name: b.name, which: k, r, v: speed(r, b.a), rv: r * speed(r, b.a)})));
  const wrap = d3.create("div");
  wrap.append(() => Plot.plot({
    title: "Orbital speed vs. distance from the Sun",
    subtitle: "Dots = closest and farthest points. Hover or tap for r × v.",
    width: width, height: 330, marginLeft: 48, marginBottom: 42,
    x: {label: "Distance from the Sun, r (AU)", type: "log", grid: true, tickFormat: d => String(+d.toFixed(2))},
    y: {label: "Speed, v (km/s)", grid: true},
    color: {domain: aoBodies.map(d => d.name), range: aoBodies.map(d => d.color), legend: true},
    marks: [
      Plot.line(curves, {x: "r", y: "v", stroke: "name", strokeWidth: 2.5}),
      Plot.dot(ends, {x: "r", y: "v", fill: "name", r: 6, stroke: "white", tip: true,
        title: d => `${d.name} (${d.which})\nr = ${d.r.toFixed(3)} AU\nv = ${d.v.toFixed(1)} km/s\nr × v = ${d.rv.toFixed(1)}`})
    ]
  }));
  wrap.append(() => html`<div style="overflow-x:auto;"><table class="ao-table">
    <thead><tr><th>Object</th><th>Closest: r × v</th><th>Farthest: r × v</th><th>Speed change</th></tr></thead>
    <tbody>${aoBodies.map(b => {
      const [c, f] = ends.filter(d => d.name === b.name);
      return html`<tr><td>${b.name}</td><td>${c.r.toFixed(3)} × ${c.v.toFixed(1)} = <strong>${c.rv.toFixed(1)}</strong></td>
        <td>${f.r.toFixed(3)} × ${f.v.toFixed(1)} = <strong>${f.rv.toFixed(1)}</strong></td><td>${f.v.toFixed(1)} → ${c.v.toFixed(1)} km/s</td></tr>`;
    })}</tbody></table></div>`);
  return wrap.node();
}
```

::: {.key-idea}
### 💡 Newton's Law of Gravitational Force

**Mathematical model:**

$$F = G\,\frac{m_1 m_2}{r^2}$$

- $F$ = force of gravity; $G$ = gravitational constant ($6.67 \times 10^{-11}$ N·m²/kg²)
- $m_1 m_2$ = mass of object 1 and mass of object 2 multiplied
- $r$ = distance between the centers of the masses

**Verbal model:** The force of gravity between two objects gets **stronger when their masses are bigger** and **much weaker as they get farther apart**: double the distance, and the force drops to **one-fourth**.

**Why objects move faster near the star:** as an object falls inward, the star's pull gets stronger ($1/r^2$) and speeds it up. As it moves outward, gravity pulls backward on it and slows it down. That's the *cause* behind Kepler's Second Law.
:::

### Who pulls hardest on Apophis?

## Part 2: Predicting Orbital Motion with Mathematical Models

Put all the laws together and you can predict an orbit completely:

| Question | Law to use | Apophis (orbit before 2029) |
|---|---|---|
| **How long** does it take to go around the Sun? | Kepler's 3rd Law: $T^2 = R^3$ (Sun) | $R = 0.922$ AU → $T = \sqrt{0.922^3} \approx 0.886$ yr (about 323 days) |
| **What path** does it take? | Kepler's 1st Law: $e = f/d$ | $d = 1.844$ AU, $f = 0.352$ AU → $e \approx 0.191$; closest 0.746 AU, farthest 1.098 AU |
| **How fast** is it moving? | Kepler's 2nd Law: $A/t = C$, $r \times v = C$ | About 37.6 km/s at 0.746 AU, slowing to 25.6 km/s at 1.098 AU |
| **Why** does it move that way? | Newton: $F = G m_1 m_2 / r^2$ | The Sun's gravity pulls it along the ellipse; nearby planets (like Earth) tug it too |

### 🗓️ Where will Apophis be on April 13, 2029?

Press **Play** or slide through time. Earth (green orbit) takes **1 year** per orbit; Apophis (red orbit) takes **0.886 years**. Because the periods are different, they line up only once in a while, and 2029 is one of those times.

Apophis's orbit is **tilted about 3.3°** compared with Earth's. Tap **Edge-on view** to see the tilt. The two orbits only come close near the line where the two orbit planes cross, which is one more reason close passes are rare.

```{ojs}

  earth: {a: [1.00000261, 0.00000562], e: [0.01671123, -0.00004392], i: [-0.00001531, -0.01294668], L: [100.46457166, 35999.37244981], longPeri: [102.93768193, 0.32327364], node: [0, 0]},
  // Real close approaches from the JPL Close Approach Data API (distance from Earth's center)
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// Two-body (Kepler) positions around the Sun, in AU, for a Julian date
aoOrbitModel = {
  const D = Math.PI / 180, TAU = 2 * Math.PI;
  const place = (a, e, i, node, argPeri, M) => {
    const E = aoSolveE(((M % TAU) + TAU) % TAU, e);
    const xp = a * (Math.cos(E) - e), yp = a * Math.sqrt(1 - e * e) * Math.sin(E);
    const cw = Math.cos(argPeri), sw = Math.sin(argPeri), cO = Math.cos(node), sO = Math.sin(node), ci = Math.cos(i), si = Math.sin(i);
    return [(cw * cO - sw * sO * ci) * xp + (-sw * cO - cw * sO * ci) * yp,
            (cw * sO + sw * cO * ci) * xp + (-sw * sO + cw * cO * ci) * yp,
            sw * si * xp + cw * si * yp];
  };
  const A = aoElements.apophis, Ea = aoElements.earth;
  const apophis = jd => place(A.a, A.e, A.i * D, A.node * D, A.peri * D, (A.M0 + A.n * (jd - A.epoch)) * D);
  const earth = jd => {
    const T = (jd - 2451545.0) / 36525, v = k => Ea[k][0] + Ea[k][1] * T;
    return place(v("a"), v("e"), v("i") * D, v("node") * D, (v("longPeri") - v("node")) * D, (v("L") - v("longPeri")) * D);
  };
  return {apophis, earth};
}
```

```{ojs}
  const fmtDate = d => new Date(Date.UTC(2021, 0, 1) + Math.round(d) * 86400000).toLocaleDateString("en-US", {timeZone: "UTC", year: "numeric", month: "short", day: "numeric"});
  const sDay = K.slider({label: "Date", min: 0, max: NDAYS, step: 1, value: 2293, fmt: fmtDate});
  const bPlay = K.button("▶ Play"), bSpeed = K.button("Speed: 40 days/s");
  const b2021 = K.button("Mar 6, 2021"), b2029 = K.button("Apr 13, 2029");
  const bTop = K.button("Top view"), bTilt = K.button("Tilted view"), bEdge = K.button("Edge-on view");
  const bIn = K.button("＋"), bOut = K.button("－");
  bIn.setAttribute("aria-label", "Zoom in"); bOut.setAttribute("aria-label", "Zoom out");
  const bCenter = K.button("Center on Earth", false), bStretch = K.button("Stretch the tilt ×5 (not real)", false);
  const rDate = K.readout("Date"), rDist = K.readout("Earth to Apophis (model)"), rSun = K.readout("Apophis: distance from Sun, speed"), rZ = K.readout("Apophis vs. Earth's orbit plane");
  const status = K.h("div", {className: "ao-sim-status", role: "status"});
  const stage = K.h("div", {className: "ao-sim-stage"});
  const labels = [["Sun", "#ffd54f"], ["Earth", "#7bed9f"], ["Apophis", "#ff8a80"]].map(([t, c]) => K.h("div", {className: "ao-sim-lab", text: t, style: `color:${c}`, "aria-hidden": "true"}));
  const root = K.h("div", {className: "ao-sim"}, [
    K.h("div", {className: "ao-sim-title", text: "3D model: the orbits of Earth and Apophis, 2021 to 2029"}),
    stage,
    K.h("div", {className: "ao-sim-btns"}, [bPlay, bSpeed, b2021, b2029]),
    sDay.row,
    K.h("div", {className: "ao-sim-btns"}, [bTop, bTilt, bEdge, bIn, bOut, bCenter, bStretch]),
    K.h("div", {className: "ao-sim-read"}, [rDate.node, rDist.node, rSun.node, rZ.node]),
    status,
    K.h("div", {className: "ao-sim-note", text: "Drag sideways on the picture to spin it (with a mouse you can also drag up and down). The Sun, Earth, and Apophis are drawn far too big so you can see them; the orbits and distances are to scale."})
  ]);

  // ---- state ----
  let day = 2293, rate = 40, az = -60, el = 38, dist = 4.3, zk = 1, center = false, drag = null;
  const orbitPts = (fn, period) => { const p = []; for (let i = 0; i < 240; i++) p.push(fn(JD0 + NDAYS - period * i / 240)); return p; };
  const earthOrbit = orbitPts(aoOrbitModel.earth, 365.256), apOrbit = orbitPts(aoOrbitModel.apophis, 360 / A.n);
  let pE = [1, 0, 0], pA = [1, 0, 0];

  // ---- renderer: three.js if WebGL works, otherwise a simple 2D drawing ----
  let gl = null, canvas, proj, paint, resize, dispose = () => {};
  if (THREE) {
    try { gl = new THREE.WebGLRenderer({antialias: true, powerPreference: "low-power"}); } catch (err) { gl = null; }
  }
  const ARIA = "3D model of the Sun with Earth's orbit in green and the orbit of asteroid Apophis in red, tilted about 3 degrees. Dots show where Earth and Apophis are on the chosen date. The values are repeated as text below.";
  if (gl) {
    canvas = gl.domElement;
    gl.setPixelRatio(Math.min(window.devicePixelRatio || 1, 2));
    gl.setClearColor(0x050816, 1);
    const scene = new THREE.Scene(), cam = new THREE.PerspectiveCamera(35, 1.4, 0.05, 200);
    cam.up.set(0, 0, 1);
    const tilted = new THREE.Group(); scene.add(tilted);       // everything that the "stretch" button scales in z
    const mat = (color, o = {}) => new THREE.MeshBasicMaterial({color, ...o});
    const tube = (pts, color, r) => new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.TubeGeometry(new THREE.CatmullRomCurve3(pts.map(p => new THREE.Vector3(...p)), true), 240, r, 6, true), mat(color));
    const tE = tube(earthOrbit, 0x2ecc71, 0.009), tA = tube(apOrbit, 0xff5252, 0.009), tA5 = tube(apOrbit.map(p => [p[0], p[1], p[2] * 5]), 0xff5252, 0.009);
    tilted.add(tE, tA, tA5);
    const disc = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.CircleGeometry(1.3, 72), mat(0x4dd0e1, {transparent: true, opacity: 0.09, side: THREE.DoubleSide, depthWrite: false}));
    scene.add(disc);
    const sun = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.SphereGeometry(0.055, 24, 16), mat(0xffc107));
    const glow = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.SphereGeometry(0.1, 24, 16), mat(0xffc107, {transparent: true, opacity: 0.25, depthWrite: false}));
    const mE = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.SphereGeometry(0.034, 20, 14), mat(0x4aa3ff));
    const mA = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.SphereGeometry(0.026, 16, 12), mat(0xffffff));
    scene.add(sun, glow, mE, mA);
    const lineGeo = new THREE.BufferGeometry(); lineGeo.setAttribute("position", new THREE.BufferAttribute(new Float32Array(6), 3));
    const link = new THREE.Line(lineGeo, new THREE.LineBasicMaterial({color: 0xffffff, transparent: true, opacity: 0.7}));
    const dropGeo = new THREE.BufferGeometry(); dropGeo.setAttribute("position", new THREE.BufferAttribute(new Float32Array(6), 3));
    const drop = new THREE.Line(dropGeo, new THREE.LineBasicMaterial({color: 0xff8a80}));
    link.frustumCulled = false; drop.frustumCulled = false;
    scene.add(link, drop);
    let seed = 987;
    const rnd = () => (seed = (seed * 16807) % 2147483647) / 2147483647;
    const sp = new Float32Array(900);
    for (let i = 0; i < 300; i++) { const t = rnd() * 2 * Math.PI, zz = rnd() * 2 - 1, q = Math.sqrt(1 - zz * zz); sp.set([60 * q * Math.cos(t), 60 * q * Math.sin(t), 60 * zz], i * 3); }
    const starGeo = new THREE.BufferGeometry(); starGeo.setAttribute("position", new THREE.BufferAttribute(sp, 3));
    scene.add(new THREE.Points(starGeo, new THREE.PointsMaterial({color: 0xffffff, size: 1.6, sizeAttenuation: false, transparent: true, opacity: 0.6})));
    const tmp = new THREE.Vector3();
    let cw = 1, ch = 1;
    resize = () => {
      cw = stage.clientWidth || 600; ch = Math.round(Math.max(250, Math.min(cw * 0.7, 440)));
      gl.setSize(cw, ch, false); canvas.style.width = "100%"; canvas.style.height = ch + "px";
      cam.aspect = cw / ch; cam.updateProjectionMatrix();
    };
    proj = p => { tmp.set(p[0], p[1], p[2] * zk).project(cam); return [(tmp.x + 1) / 2 * cw, (1 - tmp.y) / 2 * ch, tmp.z < 1]; };
    paint = () => {
      tA.visible = zk === 1; tA5.visible = zk !== 1;
      const bs = Math.max(0.5, Math.min(1.3, dist / 4.3));
      for (const o of [sun, glow, mE, mA]) o.scale.setScalar(bs);
      mE.position.set(pE[0], pE[1], pE[2] * zk); mA.position.set(pA[0], pA[1], pA[2] * zk);
      lineGeo.attributes.position.array.set([pE[0], pE[1], pE[2] * zk, pA[0], pA[1], pA[2] * zk]); lineGeo.attributes.position.needsUpdate = true;
      dropGeo.attributes.position.array.set([pA[0], pA[1], pA[2] * zk, pA[0], pA[1], 0]); dropGeo.attributes.position.needsUpdate = true;
      const t = center ? [pE[0], pE[1], pE[2] * zk] : [0, 0, 0], ce = Math.cos(el * D);
      cam.position.set(t[0] + dist * ce * Math.cos(az * D), t[1] + dist * ce * Math.sin(az * D), t[2] + dist * Math.sin(el * D));
      cam.lookAt(t[0], t[1], t[2]);
      cam.updateMatrixWorld();
      gl.render(scene, cam);
    };
    dispose = () => { scene.traverse(o => { if (o.geometry) o.geometry.dispose(); if (o.material) o.material.dispose(); }); gl.dispose(); };
  } else {
    // 2D fallback (no WebGL, or three.js could not load): same model, drawn with a simple projection
    canvas = K.h("canvas");
    const ctx = canvas.getContext("2d");
    let cw = 1, ch = 1, sc = 1, t = [0, 0, 0];
    resize = () => {
      cw = stage.clientWidth || 600; ch = Math.round(Math.max(250, Math.min(cw * 0.7, 440)));
      const dpr = Math.min(window.devicePixelRatio || 1, 2);
      canvas.width = Math.round(cw * dpr); canvas.height = Math.round(ch * dpr);
      canvas.style.width = "100%"; canvas.style.height = ch + "px";
      ctx.setTransform(dpr, 0, 0, dpr, 0, 0);
    };
    proj = p => {
      const ca = Math.cos(az * D), sa = Math.sin(az * D), ce = Math.cos(el * D), se = Math.sin(el * D);
      const x = p[0] - t[0], y = p[1] - t[1], z = p[2] * zk - t[2];
      return [cw / 2 + (-sa * x + ca * y) * sc, ch / 2 - (-se * ca * x - se * sa * y + ce * z) * sc, true];
    };
    paint = () => {
      t = center ? [pE[0], pE[1], pE[2] * zk] : [0, 0, 0];
      sc = Math.min(cw, ch * 1.3) / (dist * 0.66);
      ctx.fillStyle = "#050816"; ctx.fillRect(0, 0, cw, ch);
      const path = (pts, color) => { ctx.strokeStyle = color; ctx.lineWidth = 2; ctx.beginPath(); pts.forEach((p, i) => { const [x, y] = proj(p); if (i) ctx.lineTo(x, y); else ctx.moveTo(x, y); }); ctx.closePath(); ctx.stroke(); };
      path(earthOrbit, "#2ecc71"); path(apOrbit, "#ff5252");
      const dot = (p, r, color) => { const [x, y] = proj(p); ctx.fillStyle = color; ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(x, y, r, 0, 7); ctx.fill(); };
      const [x1, y1] = proj(pE), [x2, y2] = proj(pA);
      ctx.strokeStyle = "rgba(255,255,255,.7)"; ctx.lineWidth = 1; ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(x1, y1); ctx.lineTo(x2, y2); ctx.stroke();
      dot([0, 0, 0], 8, "#ffc107"); dot(pE, 6, "#4aa3ff"); dot(pA, 4.5, "#fff");
    };
    root.append(K.h("div", {className: "ao-sim-note", text: "Your device could not start 3D graphics, so this is a simpler flat drawing of the same model. All the buttons and numbers still work."}));
  }
  canvas.setAttribute("role", "img");
  canvas.setAttribute("aria-label", ARIA);
  stage.append(canvas, ...labels);

  function draw() {
    const jd = JD0 + day;
    pE = aoOrbitModel.earth(jd); pA = aoOrbitModel.apophis(jd);
    paint();
    [[0, 0, 0], pE, pA].forEach((p, i) => {
      const [x, y, ok] = proj(p), lab = labels[i];
      lab.style.display = ok ? "" : "none";
      lab.style.transform = `translate(${Math.round(x + 9)}px, ${Math.round(y + (i === 1 ? -22 : 6))}px)`;
    });
    const d = Math.hypot(pA[0] - pE[0], pA[1] - pE[1], pA[2] - pE[2]);
    const r = Math.hypot(pA[0], pA[1], pA[2]), v = 29.78 * Math.sqrt(2 / r - 1 / A.a);
    rDate.set(fmtDate(day));
    rDist.set(d < 0.01 ? "less than 0.01 AU" : `${d.toFixed(3)} AU = ${(d * AUKM / 1e6).toFixed(1)} million km`);
    rSun.set(`${r.toFixed(3)} AU, ${v.toFixed(1)} km/s`);
    const zkm = pA[2] * AUKM / 1e6;
    rZ.set(`${Math.abs(zkm).toFixed(1)} million km ${zkm >= 0 ? "above (north)" : "below (south)"}`);
    status.textContent = d < 0.01
      ? `Flyby! This simple model cannot work out the final distance. The real value, from NASA/JPL: ${aoElements.real2029.km.toLocaleString("en-US")} km from Earth's center on ${aoElements.real2029.date}.`
      : `That is about ${Math.round(d * AUKM / MOONKM).toLocaleString("en-US")} times the Moon's distance from Earth.`;
  }
  let pending = 0;
  const request = () => { if (!pending) pending = requestAnimationFrame(() => { pending = 0; draw(); }); };
  const stopPlay = () => { run.pause(); bPlay.textContent = "▶ Play"; };
  const run = K.runner(root, dt => {
    day += rate * dt;
    if (day >= NDAYS) { day = NDAYS; stopPlay(); }
    sDay.value = Math.round(day);
  }, () => { resize(); draw(); }, invalidation);
  bPlay.onclick = () => {
    if (run.playing) return stopPlay();
    if (day >= NDAYS) day = 0;
    run.play(); bPlay.textContent = "⏸ Pause";
  };
  bSpeed.onclick = () => { rate = rate === 40 ? 160 : rate === 160 ? 10 : 40; bSpeed.textContent = `Speed: ${rate} days/s`; };
  const jump = d => { stopPlay(); day = d; sDay.value = d; request(); };
  b2021.onclick = () => jump(64); b2029.onclick = () => jump(NDAYS);
  sDay.input.addEventListener("input", () => { stopPlay(); day = sDay.value; request(); });
  bTop.onclick = () => { el = 89.5; request(); };
  bTilt.onclick = () => { el = 38; az = -60; request(); };
  bEdge.onclick = () => { el = 0; az = A.node; request(); };     // look along the line where the two orbit planes cross
  bIn.onclick = () => { dist = Math.max(0.5, dist * 0.75); request(); };
  bOut.onclick = () => { dist = Math.min(6, dist / 0.75); request(); };
  bCenter.onclick = () => { center = !center; bCenter.setAttribute("aria-pressed", String(center)); request(); };
  bStretch.onclick = () => { zk = zk === 1 ? 5 : 1; bStretch.setAttribute("aria-pressed", String(zk === 5)); request(); };
  canvas.addEventListener("pointerdown", e => { drag = {x: e.clientX, y: e.clientY, az, el}; try { canvas.setPointerCapture(e.pointerId); } catch (err) {} canvas.style.cursor = "grabbing"; });
  canvas.addEventListener("pointermove", e => {
    if (!drag) return;
    az = drag.az - (e.clientX - drag.x) * 0.45;
    if (e.pointerType !== "touch") el = Math.max(-89.5, Math.min(89.5, drag.el + (e.clientY - drag.y) * 0.45));
    request();
  });
  const endDrag = () => { drag = null; canvas.style.cursor = ""; };
  canvas.addEventListener("pointerup", endDrag); canvas.addEventListener("pointercancel", endDrag);
  invalidation.then(() => { if (pending) cancelAnimationFrame(pending); dispose(); });
  resize(); draw();
  return root;
}
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## 📊 Where the numbers in this model come from

- **Apophis's orbit:** real orbital elements from NASA/JPL's [Small-Body Database](https://ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/tools/sbdb_lookup.html#/?sstr=99942) (orbit solution 220, epoch June 9, 2026): average distance 0.9224 AU, eccentricity 0.1911, tilt 3.341°, period 323.6 days.
- **Earth's orbit:** JPL's [Approximate Positions of the Planets](https://ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/planets/approx_pos.html) (Earth-Moon system, valid 1800 to 2050).
- **Real close approaches:** JPL's [Close Approach Data](https://cneos.jpl.nasa.gov/ca/): 0.113 AU on March 6, 2021 and 38,012 km from Earth's center on April 13, 2029.
- **What the model leaves out:** it is a **simplified two-body model**. Each object feels only the Sun's gravity, exactly as Kepler's laws describe. It ignores the small tugs from the planets. From 2021 to 2029 its Earth-to-Apophis distances stay within a few percent of JPL's full calculation, but it is **not** precise enough to give the final flyby distance, so the model does not show one. The model stops on April 13, 2029, because Earth's gravity changes Apophis's orbit that day.
:::

::: {.callout-important}
## 🎯 Why precision matters

On the scale of this model, Apophis's real 2029 miss distance (about 38,000 km from Earth's center) is **much smaller than one pixel**. A tiny error in the orbit would turn a "miss" into a "hit" on paper. That's why scientists keep measuring Apophis with telescopes and radar, and why each new measurement improves the prediction.
:::

::: {.student-task}
### ✏️ In your packet: Part 2 + your Apophis model

- **Q1–3:** How can we predict **how long** an object takes to orbit the Sun? **How fast** it's traveling? **What path** it takes? (Hint: one law answers each.)
- **Q4:** What's missing? Even though we know *what* is happening, do we know *why*? (Think: gravity.)
- **Model:** Draw a model explaining how Kepler's Laws and gravity let us predict Apophis's path. **Annotate** it so it explains how we know where Apophis will be on **April 13, 2029**.
:::

## Summary Task

::: {.student-task}
### ✏️ In your packet: Summary Task

**Q5:** How are Kepler's Laws used to make predictions about whether Apophis will orbit near Earth?

*Think about:* the **period** (3rd Law) tells *when* Apophis returns to the same part of its orbit; the **shape** (1st Law) tells *how close* its path comes to Earth's orbit; the **speed** (2nd Law) tells *where along the path* it is at a given time; and **gravity** explains all three.
:::

# Elaborate: Will Apophis Hit Earth in the 2030s?

::: {.elaborate-box}
## 🌍 Earth's Gravity Will Bend Apophis's Path

Apophis will miss Earth on April 13, 2029. But it will pass so close that **Earth's gravity will change its trajectory**. Scientists asked: *could that change put Apophis on a path to collide with Earth in the 2030s?*
:::

During the flyby, Earth's pull (about 46× the Sun's) acts on Apophis for several hours. The closer the pass, the stronger the pull, and the more the path bends. Change the **closest distance** and watch the path. The **dashed line** is where Apophis would go with no Earth gravity; the **yellow angle** is how much the path bends.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof fbDist = {
  const K = aoKit, W = 360, H = 270, TAU = 2 * Math.PI;
  const MU = 398600.4, VINF = 5.84;       // Earth's GM (km³/s²); Apophis's approach speed far from Earth (km/s, JPL)
  const RE = 6371, GEO = 42164, MOON = 384400, LO = 7000, HI = 400000;
  const cv = K.canvas2d(W, H, "Animated model of Apophis flying past Earth. The red curved path bends toward Earth. A dashed gray line shows the straight path it would take with no gravity.");
  const ctx = cv.ctx;
  const toRp = t => { const v = LO * Math.pow(HI / LO, t / 1000); return Math.min(HI, Math.max(LO, Math.round(v / 500) * 500)); };
  const toT = rp => 1000 * Math.log(rp / LO) / Math.log(HI / LO);
  const sD = K.slider({label: "Closest distance from Earth's center (km)", min: 0, max: 1000, step: 1, value: toT(38000), fmt: t => toRp(t).toLocaleString("en-US") + " km"});
  sD.input.setAttribute("aria-valuetext", "38,000 km");
  const bPlay = K.button(K.reduce ? "▶ Play" : "⏸ Pause");
  const bA = K.button("Apophis 2029: 38,000 km"), bG = K.button("10× farther: 380,000 km"), bC = K.button("Very close: 10,000 km");
  const rB = K.readout("Path bent by"), rT = K.readout("Time from closest point"), rR = K.readout("Distance from Earth's center now"), rV = K.readout("Speed compared with Earth now");
  const root = K.h("div", {className: "ao-sim"}, [
    K.h("div", {className: "ao-sim-title", text: "Model: Earth's gravity bends the flyby path"}),
    cv.c,
    K.h("div", {className: "ao-sim-btns"}, [bPlay, bA, bG, bC]),
    sD.row,
    K.h("div", {className: "ao-sim-read"}, [rB.node, rT.node, rR.node, rV.node]),
    K.h("div", {className: "ao-sim-note", text: "This is a what-if model with only two objects: Earth and Apophis. It uses Apophis's real approach speed (5.84 km/s far from Earth, from NASA/JPL) and Earth's real gravity. Only the 38,000 km pass is the real 2029 flyby. Earth and the distances are drawn to scale; the picture zooms to fit."})
  ]);
  let rp = 38000, u = 0.5;
  root.value = rp;

  function orbit() {
    const a = MU / (VINF * VINF), e = 1 + rp / a, b = a * Math.sqrt(e * e - 1);
    const bend = 2 * Math.asin(1 / e), phi = bend / 2 - Math.PI / 2, n = Math.sqrt(MU / (a * a * a));
    return {a, e, b, bend, phi, n};
  }
  function draw() {
    cv.fit();
    const o = orbit(), s = 70 / o.b, EX = 196, EY = 122;
    const cp = Math.cos(o.phi), sp = Math.sin(o.phi);
    const scr = (xp, yp) => [EX + (xp * cp - yp * sp) * s, EY - (xp * sp + yp * cp) * s];
    const at = Hh => scr(o.a * (o.e - Math.cosh(Hh)), o.b * Math.sinh(Hh));
    ctx.fillStyle = "#0a0a2e"; ctx.fillRect(0, 0, W, H);
    K.stars(ctx, W, H);
    ctx.font = "10.5px sans-serif"; ctx.textBaseline = "alphabetic";
    // reference rings (real distances from Earth's center)
    for (const [km, label] of [[GEO, "Geostationary satellites"], [MOON, "Moon's distance"]]) {
      const rr = km * s;
      if (rr < 9 || rr > 330) continue;
      ctx.strokeStyle = "rgba(116,185,255,.55)"; ctx.setLineDash([2, 4]); ctx.lineWidth = 1;
      ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(EX, EY, rr, 0, TAU); ctx.stroke(); ctx.setLineDash([]);
      ctx.fillStyle = "rgba(160,205,255,.95)"; ctx.textAlign = "center";
      if (EY - rr > 22) ctx.fillText(label, EX, EY - rr - 4);
      else { ctx.textAlign = "right"; ctx.fillText(label, W - 6, Math.min(H - 8, EY + Math.sqrt(Math.max(rr * rr - (W - 40 - EX) ** 2, 0)) + 14)); }
    }
    // straight path with no gravity (dashed)
    const yIn = EY + o.b * s;
    ctx.strokeStyle = "#9aa7bd"; ctx.setLineDash([5, 4]); ctx.lineWidth = 1.3;
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(0, yIn); ctx.lineTo(W, yIn); ctx.stroke(); ctx.setLineDash([]);
    // bend angle marker where the incoming and outgoing directions cross
    const [qx, qy] = scr(o.a * o.e, 0);
    ctx.strokeStyle = "rgba(255,255,255,.35)"; ctx.lineWidth = 1; ctx.setLineDash([2, 3]);
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(qx, qy); ctx.lineTo(qx + 400 * Math.cos(o.bend), qy - 400 * Math.sin(o.bend)); ctx.stroke(); ctx.setLineDash([]);
    ctx.strokeStyle = "#ffd54f"; ctx.lineWidth = 2;
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(qx, qy, 34, -o.bend, 0); ctx.stroke();
    ctx.fillStyle = "#ffd54f"; ctx.font = "bold 11px sans-serif"; ctx.textAlign = "left";
    ctx.fillText((o.bend * 180 / Math.PI).toFixed(1) + "°", Math.min(qx + 40, W - 40), qy - Math.max(9, 17 * Math.sin(o.bend / 2)) + 1);
    // the real (curved) path
    const Hmax = Math.acosh((5.2 * o.b / o.a + 1) / o.e);
    ctx.strokeStyle = "#ff5252"; ctx.lineWidth = 2.4; ctx.beginPath();
    for (let i = 0; i <= 160; i++) { const [px, py] = at(-Hmax + 2 * Hmax * i / 160); if (i) ctx.lineTo(px, py); else ctx.moveTo(px, py); }
    ctx.stroke();
    // Earth, to scale
    const er = RE * s;
    ctx.fillStyle = "#2e86de"; ctx.strokeStyle = "#7bed9f"; ctx.lineWidth = er > 4 ? 1.5 : 0.8;
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(EX, EY, Math.max(er, 1.6), 0, TAU); ctx.fill(); ctx.stroke();
    ctx.fillStyle = "#fff"; ctx.font = "bold 11px sans-serif"; ctx.textAlign = "center";
    ctx.fillText("Earth", EX, EY - Math.max(er, 1.6) - 5);
    // Apophis now
    const tmax = (o.e * Math.sinh(Hmax) - Hmax) / o.n, t = -tmax + 2 * tmax * u, Mh = o.n * t;
    let Hh = Math.asinh(Mh / o.e);
    for (let i = 0; i < 25; i++) Hh -= (o.e * Math.sinh(Hh) - Hh - Mh) / (o.e * Math.cosh(Hh) - 1);
    const [ax, ay] = at(Hh), r = o.a * (o.e * Math.cosh(Hh) - 1), v = Math.sqrt(VINF * VINF + 2 * MU / r);
    ctx.strokeStyle = "rgba(255,255,255,.3)"; ctx.lineWidth = 1; ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(EX, EY); ctx.lineTo(ax, ay); ctx.stroke();
    ctx.fillStyle = "#fff"; ctx.strokeStyle = "#ff5252"; ctx.lineWidth = 2;
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(ax, ay, 4.5, 0, TAU); ctx.fill(); ctx.stroke();
    ctx.fillStyle = "#ffb3b3"; ctx.font = "bold 11px sans-serif"; ctx.textAlign = ax > W - 60 ? "right" : "left";
    ctx.fillText("Apophis", ax + (ax > W - 60 ? -8 : 8), ay - 8);
    ctx.fillStyle = "#c0c9e2"; ctx.font = "10.5px sans-serif"; ctx.textAlign = "left";
    ctx.fillText("Dashed: path with no Earth gravity", 8, Math.min(yIn + 14, H - 6));
    // scale bar
    const nice = [1000, 2000, 5000, 10000, 20000, 50000, 100000, 200000, 500000].find(k => k * s >= 36) || 500000;
    ctx.strokeStyle = "#e2e8f0"; ctx.lineWidth = 2; ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(10, 14); ctx.lineTo(10 + nice * s, 14); ctx.stroke();
    ctx.fillStyle = "#e2e8f0"; ctx.fillText(nice.toLocaleString("en-US") + " km", 15 + nice * s, 17);
    const hrs = t / 3600, ah = Math.abs(hrs);
    rB.set((o.bend * 180 / Math.PI).toFixed(1) + "°");
    rT.set(ah < 0.05 ? "closest point" : (ah >= 48 ? (ah / 24).toFixed(1) + " days " : ah.toFixed(1) + " hours ") + (hrs < 0 ? "before" : "after"));
    rR.set((Math.round(r / 100) * 100).toLocaleString("en-US") + " km");
    rV.set(v.toFixed(2) + " km/s");
  }
  const run = K.runner(root, dt => { u += dt / 9; if (u > 1) u = 0; }, draw, invalidation);
  bPlay.onclick = () => { if (run.playing) { run.pause(); bPlay.textContent = "▶ Play"; } else { run.play(); bPlay.textContent = "⏸ Pause"; } };
  const setRp = (v, fromSlider) => {
    rp = v; root.value = rp;
    if (!fromSlider) { sD.value = toT(rp); root.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", {bubbles: true})); }
    sD.input.setAttribute("aria-valuetext", rp.toLocaleString("en-US") + " km");
    draw();
  };
  sD.input.addEventListener("input", () => setRp(toRp(sD.value), true));
  bA.onclick = () => setRp(38000); bG.onclick = () => setRp(380000); bC.onclick = () => setRp(10000);
  draw();
  if (!K.reduce) run.play();
  return root;
}
```

::: {.key-idea}
### 💡 Gravity changes trajectories, and a changed path is a new orbit

- Earth's pull bends Apophis's path by roughly **27°** (model estimate) and changes its speed relative to the Sun.
- A new speed and direction means a **new orbit**: Apophis's average distance will grow from about **0.92 AU to about 1.1 AU**, so its **period** gets longer (Kepler's Third Law), from about **0.89 years to about 1.16 years**.
- If Apophis passed through a tiny region near Earth called a **gravitational keyhole**, the bend would put it on a new orbit that brings it back to Earth years later. In the 2000s a keyhole leading to a **2036** impact was a real concern.
- Better measurements (especially **radar in 2021**) showed Apophis will **not** pass through any dangerous keyhole. NASA has ruled out an impact for **at least 100 years**.
- Scientists keep watching because tiny forces (like sunlight warming one side and pushing it, called the **Yarkovsky effect**) slowly shift asteroid orbits too.
:::

```{ojs}
  }
```

# Evaluate: Deflecting Asteroids

::: {.evaluate-box}
## 🚀 The Gravity Tractor

Scientists are confident Apophis won't hit Earth, but some asteroid someday might change paths and threaten our planet. One idea is a **gravity tractor**: a spacecraft that **hovers next to an asteroid** and uses its **own gravity** to slowly pull the asteroid off course. No touching, no explosions, just $F = G m_1 m_2 / r^2$.
:::

::: {.key-idea}
### 💡 How a gravity tractor works

1. A heavy spacecraft flies alongside the asteroid and **hovers** a few hundred meters away.
2. The spacecraft and asteroid **attract each other** by gravity.
3. The spacecraft fires its thrusters (angled so the exhaust misses the asteroid) to stay in place, so it keeps **towing** the asteroid.
4. The tiny tug, applied for **years**, changes the asteroid's speed a little. A slightly different speed means a **different orbit** (Kepler's laws), so it arrives at Earth's orbit at a different time and **misses**.
:::

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
```
```{ojs}
{
  const G = 6.674e-11, yr = 3.156e7;
  const m = gtSc * 1000, r = gtHover * gtAst.radius;
  const F = G * m * gtAst.mass / (r * r);       // newtons
  const acc = F / gtAst.mass;                    // m/s², = G m / r² (asteroid mass cancels!)
  const dv = acc * gtYears * yr;                 // m/s
  const shift = 0.5 * acc * (gtYears * yr) ** 2 / 1000;   // km, simple straight-line estimate
  const series = d3.range(0, gtYears + 0.01, gtYears / 60).map(y => ({y, km: 0.5 * acc * (y * yr) ** 2 / 1000}));
  const wrap = d3.create("div");
  wrap.append("div").style("padding", "12px 16px").style("border-radius", "10px").style("margin-bottom", "8px")
    .style("background", "rgba(0,131,143,0.1)").style("border-left", "4px solid #00838f")
    .html(`<div>Hover distance: <strong>${Math.round(r)} m</strong> from the asteroid's center</div>
      <div>Gravity force: F = G·m₁·m₂/r² ≈ <strong>${F.toFixed(2)} N</strong> (about the weight of ${F < 1 ? "a small apple or less" : F < 10 ? "a bag of apples" : "a heavy backpack"})</div>
      <div>Asteroid's speed change after ${gtYears} yr: <strong>${(dv * 1000).toFixed(1)} mm/s</strong></div>
      <div>Rough shift in position: <strong>${Math.round(shift).toLocaleString()} km</strong> (${(shift / 6371).toFixed(2)} Earth radii)</div>`);
  wrap.append(() => Plot.plot({
    title: "A tiny tug adds up over time",
    subtitle: "Rough straight-line estimate; real orbital effects can make the shift several times larger",
    width: width, height: 260, marginLeft: 60, marginBottom: 40, marginRight: 16,
    x: {label: "Years of towing", grid: true},
    y: {label: "Shift in position (km)", grid: true},
    marks: [
      Plot.areaY(series, {x: "y", y: "km", fill: "#00838f", fillOpacity: 0.2}),
      Plot.line(series, {x: "y", y: "km", stroke: "#00838f", strokeWidth: 2.5}),
      Plot.ruleY([6371], {stroke: "#d63031", strokeDasharray: "5,4"}),
      Plot.text([6371], {x: 0, y: d => d, text: () => "Earth's radius (6,371 km)", dy: -7, textAnchor: "start", fill: "#d63031", fontSize: 10})
    ]
  }));
  return wrap.node();
}
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## ➕ Optional Extension: DART, a different way to deflect

In **September 2022**, NASA's **DART** spacecraft crashed into **Dimorphos**, a small moon of asteroid Didymos. The impact shortened Dimorphos's orbit around Didymos by about **33 minutes**, proving that a spacecraft *can* change an asteroid's orbit. DART is a fast "push"; a gravity tractor is a slow, steady "pull" that can be steered very precisely.
:::

|---|---|

# Chapter Summary

| Key Concept | Details |
|---|---|
| **Where asteroids come from** | Leftovers from solar system formation; most orbit in the main belt between Mars and Jupiter |
| **Near-Earth asteroids** | Over 35,000 known; ~95% of 1 km+ found, fewer than half of 140 m+ found |
| **Kepler's First Law (review)** | Orbits are ellipses; $e = f/d$; closest $= R(1-e)$, farthest $= R(1+e)$ |
| **Kepler's Second Law** | Equal areas in equal times: $A/t = C$. Distance × speed stays constant: closer → faster |
| **Kepler's Third Law (review)** | $M_s \times T^2 = R^3$; for our Sun $T^2 = R^3$ |
| **Newton's Law of Gravitational Force** | $F = G\,m_1 m_2 / r^2$: more mass → stronger; double the distance → ¼ the force |
| **Apophis** | ~340 m; orbit 0.746–1.098 AU, $e \approx 0.19$, $T \approx 0.886$ yr; passes ~32,000 km above Earth on April 13, 2029 |
| **Flyby effect** | Earth's pull (~46× the Sun's) bends the path ~27° and gives Apophis a new, larger orbit |
| **Gravity tractor** | A hovering spacecraft's gravity tows an asteroid; tiny force, so it needs years of warning |

```{=html}
    el('aomf-next').style.display = 'none';
    el('aomf-myth').disabled = false;
    el('aomf-fact').disabled = false;
    el('aomf-myth').style.opacity = '1';
    el('aomf-fact').style.opacity = '1';
    cardAnswered = false;
  }
  window.aomfAnswer = function(choice) {
    if (cardAnswered) return;
    cardAnswered = true;
    answered++;
    var card = cards[idx];
    var correct = (choice === card.type);
    if (correct) score++;
    el('aomf-score').textContent = score;
    el('aomf-total').textContent = answered;
    var fb = el('aomf-feedback');
    fb.style.display = 'block';
    fb.style.background = correct ? 'rgba(0,184,148,0.2)' : 'rgba(214,48,49,0.2)';
    fb.style.border = '1px solid ' + (correct ? '#00b894' : '#e17055');
    fb.innerHTML = '<strong>' + (correct ? '✅ Correct! ' : '❌ That\'s a ' + card.type + '! ') + '</strong>' + card.explanation;
    el('aomf-myth').disabled = true;
    el('aomf-fact').disabled = true;
    el('aomf-myth').style.opacity = (choice === 'Myth') ? '1' : '0.5';
    el('aomf-fact').style.opacity = (choice === 'Fact') ? '1' : '0.5';
    el('aomf-next').style.display = 'block';
  };
  window.aomfNext = function() { idx++; updateCard(); };
  window.aomfRestart = function() {
    idx = 0; score = 0; answered = 0;
    el('aomf-card').style.display = 'flex';
    el('aomf-myth').style.display = 'block';
    el('aomf-fact').style.display = 'block';
    el('aomf-done').style.display = 'none';
    el('aomf-score').textContent = '0';
    el('aomf-total').textContent = '0';
    updateCard();
  };
  updateCard();
})();
</script>
```

# End-of-Chapter Quiz

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
function buildAsteroidQuiz(id, title, questions) {
  const outer = html`<div id="${id}" style="font-family:'Inter',sans-serif; max-width:720px; margin:18px auto;"></div>`;
  const header = html`<div style="background:linear-gradient(135deg,#667eea 0%,#764ba2 100%);color:#fff;border-radius:14px 14px 0 0;padding:18px 24px;">
    <div style="font-size:1.1em;font-weight:700;display:flex;align-items:center;gap:8px;"><span style="font-size:1.2em;">📝</span> ${title}</div>
    <div style="font-size:0.85em;opacity:0.85;margin-top:4px;">Select an answer for each question.</div>
  </div>`;
  const body = html`<div style="border:1.5px solid #c7d2fe;border-top:none;border-radius:0 0 14px 14px;overflow:hidden;background:#f8f9ff;padding:16px;"></div>`;
  questions.forEach((qq, qi) => {
    const card = document.createElement("div");
    card.style.cssText = "background:#fff;color:#1e1b4b;border-radius:12px;padding:16px 20px;margin-bottom:14px;box-shadow:0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,.08);";
    card.innerHTML = `<p style="font-weight:700;margin:0 0 10px;color:#1e1b4b;">${qi+1}. ${qq.q}</p>`;
    qq.options.forEach((opt, oi) => {
      const btn = document.createElement("button");
      btn.textContent = opt;
      btn.style.cssText = "display:block;width:100%;min-height:44px;text-align:left;padding:10px 14px;margin:6px 0;border:2px solid #e2e8f0;border-radius:8px;background:#fff;color:#1e1b4b;cursor:pointer;font-size:.95em;transition:border-color .2s,background .2s;";
      btn.onmouseover = () => { if(!card.dataset.answered){ btn.style.borderColor="#667eea";btn.style.background="#f0f0ff"; }};
      btn.onmouseout  = () => { if(!card.dataset.answered){ btn.style.borderColor="#e2e8f0";btn.style.background="#fff"; }};
      btn.onclick = () => {
        if(card.dataset.answered) return;
        card.dataset.answered = "true";
        card.querySelectorAll("button").forEach(b => {
          b.style.cursor="default"; b.onmouseover=null; b.onmouseout=null;
          b.style.borderColor="#e2e8f0"; b.style.background="#f8fafc"; b.style.color="#475569";
        });
        if(oi === qq.correct){
          btn.style.borderColor="#48bb78";btn.style.background="#f0fff4";btn.style.color="#276749";btn.style.fontWeight="700";
          fb.innerHTML = "✅ Correct! " + qq.explanation;
          fb.style.color="#276749";fb.style.background="#f0fff4";
        } else {
          btn.style.borderColor="#fc8181";btn.style.background="#fff5f5";btn.style.color="#9b2c2c";btn.style.fontWeight="700";
          const correctBtn = card.querySelectorAll("button")[qq.correct];
          correctBtn.style.borderColor="#48bb78";correctBtn.style.background="#f0fff4";correctBtn.style.color="#276749";correctBtn.style.fontWeight="700";
          fb.innerHTML = "❌ " + qq.explanation;
          fb.style.color="#9b2c2c";fb.style.background="#fff5f5";
        }
        fb.style.padding="10px 14px";fb.style.marginTop="8px";fb.style.borderRadius="8px";
      };
      card.appendChild(btn);
    });
    const fb = document.createElement("div");
    fb.style.cssText = "border-radius:8px;font-size:.9em;transition:all .3s;";
    card.appendChild(fb);
    body.appendChild(card);
  });
  outer.appendChild(header);
  outer.appendChild(body);
  return outer;
}
```

```{ojs}
  },

    options: ["It changes a lot", "It stays constant, because its distance from the Sun never changes", "It is zero", "It is fastest at aphelion"],
    correct: 1,
    explanation: "e = 0 is a circle, so r never changes. Since r × v stays constant, v stays constant too."
  },
  {
    q: "Using r × v = constant: an asteroid moves at 20 km/s at 2 AU. How fast is it moving when it is at 1 AU (on the same orbit's closest/farthest points)?",
    options: ["10 km/s", "20 km/s", "40 km/s", "80 km/s"],
    correct: 2,
    explanation: "r × v = 2 × 20 = 40. At r = 1 AU, v = 40 ÷ 1 = 40 km/s. Half the distance → twice the speed."
  },
  {
    q: "Two asteroids have the same mass. Asteroid A is 3 times farther from a planet than asteroid B. Compared with B, the planet's pull on A is…",
    options: ["3 times stronger", "1/3 as strong", "1/9 as strong", "The same"],
    correct: 2,
    explanation: "F ∝ 1/r². Three times the distance → 1/3² = 1/9 of the force."
  },
  {
    q: "In the Gravity and Orbits simulation, the star's mass increases so the planet's orbit becomes an ellipse. Where along the ellipse is the gravity force strongest and the velocity greatest?",
    options: ["At the point closest to the star", "At the point farthest from the star", "Halfway between", "Gravity and velocity are the same everywhere"],
    correct: 0,
    explanation: "Closest point → smallest r → biggest force (1/r²). The pull has been speeding the planet up as it falls inward, so it's also moving fastest there."
  },
  {
    q: "Apophis's average distance is 0.922 AU. About how long does one orbit take?",
    options: ["0.886 years", "1.0 year", "0.85 days", "2.2 years"],
    correct: 0,
    explanation: "Kepler's Third Law for our Sun: T = √(R³) = √(0.922³) ≈ 0.886 years (about 323 days)."
  },

    explanation: "e = f ÷ d = 0.352 ÷ 1.844 ≈ 0.19. Closest = 0.922 × (1 − 0.19) ≈ 0.75 AU, farthest ≈ 1.10 AU, so its path crosses Earth's orbit at 1 AU."
  },
  {

    correct: 0,
    explanation: "Earth's gravity changes the orbit during the flyby. Passing through a tiny keyhole would have set up a future impact. Precise 2021 radar data showed that won't happen."
  },

  }
```
